messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proxying & handshake for subprocessor localization — TIA scope request

Team —

Quick summary: ClearCare (prospect, enterprise health customer) has asked for a pragmatic onshore fallback for EU patient-identifiable payloads while they complete their procurement for a full UK Addendum / DTIA path. They want to understand whether we can support a proxying architecture (onshore edge + Redwood-hosted encrypted KV cache) and which subprocessors will touch derived telemetry.

Why it matters: legal wants clear evidence of (1) which subprocessors process residues of EU PII, (2) what the TIA/DTIA scope would be for the proxying option, and (3) whether the UK IDTA / SCC mapping will be materially different under the proxying fallback. Procurement will push for a single-sourced warranty and narrower subprocessors list if possible.

Asks:
- Kimberly: can you draft a short note on whether proxying + ephemeral onshore cache meets our current SCCs + UK IDTA stance (i.e., equivalent safeguards + encryption at rest/in transit)? Bullet points are fine.
- Marissa: we need the subprocessor-impact statement for the sales pack (one-pager). I will request their full subprocessor CSV and TIA form — please prepare a redline checklist for the DPA addendum we’ll likely propose.
- Laura: legal — flag any ‘deal killer’ terms you foresee in the fallback (e.g., escrow/escrowed logs, residency SLA, audit rights).

I’ll reach out to the customer for the subprocessor CSV and the filled TIA form. Aim: keep commercial momentum by offering a documented fallback that closes procurement questions within 7 business days.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@clearcarehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: next steps for DPA / TIA evidence (ClearCare)

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attaching a short TIA scope form (Cardinal_TIA_Scope_Form.pdf) and a checklist of what will help our legal team evaluate the UK Addendum / SCC equivalence. Please send:
- Your current subprocessors list (CSV preferred)
- Any signed UK Addendum / IDTA drafts you have on file
- Timeline constraints for procurement (target sign date)

To be explicit about the technical option we discussed:
- Option A (default): Redwood serves from EU region; existing SCCs / UK Addendum apply.
- Option B (fallback/proxying): ClearCare routes select PII to an onshore proxy endpoint (customer-controlled), Redwood stores only encrypted KV prefixes for inference results. We need to validate whether the proxying approach maintains parity with SCC/UKIDTA assurances for audit logs and subprocessors.

Attachments referenced (please attach when you reply): clearcare-subprocessors.csv, any redline notes, and the signed UK addendum if available.

If it helps we can set a 30-min call with legal and infra tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Markus

Attachment stubs: [Cardinal_TIA_Scope_Form.pdf] (fillable TIA scope spreadsheet)

Cc: partners@globalproxy.io
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:33:00 +0100
Subject: Re: next steps for DPA / TIA evidence (ClearCare)

Hi Markus —

Thanks — attaching the subprocessors file and a short note from our security team.

Key points from ClearCare security:
- We have a signed UK Addendum in process (DocuSign envelope attached) but not yet fully executed; legal expects the signed copy before final DPA sign-off.
- For the short term we can accept a regional proxying model for limited data classes (PHI identifiers used only for matching) provided: (a) Redwood can prove subprocessors list and provide certificate-of-encryption for the KV cache, (b) audit logs for the onshore proxy are retained for 30 days and available to our auditors on request.
- We flagged two subprocessors in your list if they will be used for model telemetry: telemetry-ops@thirdparty.io (they do inference-level metrics) and metrics-store@observability.co (they store aggregated logs). Both need scoping.

Attachments: clearcare-subprocessors.csv, signed-ukaddendum-docusign-link.txt (DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope12345), security_note_short.pdf

On the proxying architecture: partners@globalproxy.io offered to provide an ephemeral onshore proxy that forwards only hashed keys; they sent an architecture diagram (proxying-architecture-diagram.png) and API integration notes.

Happy to take a call with your legal and infra. Do you have midday CET tomorrow?

— Emma
VP, Procurement & Security
ClearCare Health Systems

Subject: Re: Proxying & handshake for subprocessor localization — TIA scope request

Markus / team —

Thanks for the thread and thanks Emma for the details. Quick internal summary and recommended next steps:

1) Technical equivalence (short): the proxying pattern can be acceptable from an SCC/UKIDTA perspective if we ensure: encryption-at-rest keys are customer-segmented (KMS), KV cache contains only non-reversible prefixes, and audit logs from the proxy are immutable and accessible. We should not commit to onshore storage of raw PII. (I asked infra for a one-page note.)

2) Subprocessor impact: the CSV flagged two telemetry providers (metrics-store@observability.co, telemetry-ops@thirdparty.io). We need vendor attestations for both: SOC2 + scope statement that they do not retain raw customer PII. Ask Marissa to prepare a vendor evidence request template.

3) Legal redlines to expect: audit-rights SLA (30-day log retention), carveouts for escrowed logs only under subpoena, explicit statement that Redwood will not export raw PII to any subprocessor outside EU unless agreed. Laura — please draft a short DPA addendum template with those bullets.

4) Customer-facing cadence: propose a 30-min legal + infra call tomorrow 10:00 CET (I can host). Markus — can you confirm with Emma? Marissa — prepare the one-pager and a short subprocessor evidence request (CSV + certs).

Action items:
- Laura: DPA addendum bullet draft (EOD Fri)
- Marissa: vendor evidence request template + sales one-pager (tomorrow morning)
- Markus: confirm call with ClearCare and partners

If all looks OK I’ll draft a short note for procurement to accept proxying as a conditional fallback (with documented evidence).

— Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
